name: Hub tier rule for a deep run
description: Starts a deep run on the tier the hub's rule gives (the person's tier or standing guidance, else the cheapest tier measured good enough), resolved to a model through the registry; an operator's start models count as standing guidance; an escalation moves one rung for one task and needs a specific reason; sub-agents default to the hub's sub-agent tier.
advantages: Follows the owner's rule in one place, names no model in code, records tier, source and reason with every run, with no additional model call.
disadvantages: Depends on the hub's measured pass rates for what is good enough; a failed check retries on a higher tier only when the verifier names what was missing.

name: Live tier registry
description: Maps a tier name to the newest live model id by bucketing a provider's latest-first list by family, caching the result, using a last-known fallback only when the live list is empty, and exposing the next lower tier and vision capability.
advantages: Tracks new releases automatically and never fails resolution when the provider is unreachable.
disadvantages: The fallback map can go stale, and bucketing by family substring depends on provider naming conventions.

name: Subscription allowance limit detector
description: Detects a subscription usage-limit message in a run's result, parses its reset time and zone, computes a resume time, and records the limit lane-wide with optional persistence so other work waits.
advantages: Resumes after the real reset instead of retrying uselessly, and survives a restart when persistence is configured.
disadvantages: Depends on parsing human-readable wording and time zones, which can change without notice.

name: Call roles over the hub's tier table
description: Binds each Quest AI Runner model call (a prompt spec id or a direct call) to a role of the hub's role table, which gives the tier, and applies a person's or lane's explicit tier under three guards: classification never above fast, a response never below balanced, best only by a person's explicit tier or the structure-watch role. Deep work defaults to balanced. The legacy word science reads as its role's tier.
advantages: One table decides every call's tier; a prompt spec cannot declare a tier the table does not give, and a new call without a role fails where it is written.
disadvantages: The hub's table rows are the owner's policy and unmeasured; a lane that sets a tier by name still moves the calls that are neither classification nor a response.
